source.edition: Third Edition and Twelfth Thousand, revised to 1878 (Rumsey composite; metadata sometimes lists 1881)
source.credit: Image: David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0)

notes: One continuous horizontal timeline (not stacked separate time bands).
Nation/empire streams are parallel horizontal colored bands that widen, thin, split, and merge.
BC centuries labeled with 2-digit marks (39 = 3900 BC) counting down left to right.
AD centuries labeled after the birth of Christ.
Scale is roughly 12.5-13 px/year but not perfectly uniform; use piecewise-linear anchors every century.
A wider gap near Flood/Babel required inserting one interpolated century pillar.
Far-right portrait and index panels sit after the linear stream ends (~1881) and are outside the year axis.
Intro maps and artifact illustrations occupy the far left near Creation.

method.summary: Detected dark century pillars on IIIF axis strips; verified with OCR/visual crops at 3700 BC, 100 BC, AD 1 (Jesus region), AD 1800, AD 1881; inserted one missing pillar in the Flood/Babel gap; trimmed false end detections; piecewise-linear interpolation.
method.accuracy: Century anchors typically within ~30-80 px (~3-7 years). Jump-to-year for mid-century points may be off by up to ~10-15 years where scale wobbles. Uncertain: exact Flood year x (chart texts cite 2348/2347 and Babel 2247); exact boundary where linear streams meet right-hand panels.
method.cors: Rumsey IIIF returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with Origin header; OpenSeadragon can stream tiles directly.
